Living Well / Resource directory

Make a small thing worth sharing

Start with life

What would be useful?

Express an idea in a form another person can encounter, with its meaning and permissions intact.

The simpler starting point: Start with a paragraph, paper sketch, or your existing editor. Choose one small finished object.

Finish when: Open the export outside the editor and confirm that it communicates accurately and accessibly.

Choose by fit

Different tools, different jobs.

These are editorial comparisons based on public descriptions, not a ranking from hands-on tests. Choose one suitable route; using every option is not the goal.

GIMP: edit an image

Consider it when: You need a photo correction or simple graphic.

Check first: Work on a copy and preserve the original.

Access: Free open-source desktop editor for supported Windows, macOS, and Linux systems.

Open GIMP: edit an image · Full context and source

Krita: draw and paint

Consider it when: You want to draw or paint rather than edit a photograph.

Check first: Start with a small canvas and a few familiar tools.

Access: Free open-source painting software from the official site. Compatible hardware is needed; store editions and optional extras may differ.

Open Krita: draw and paint · Full context and source

Twine: an interactive story

Consider it when: The idea works through choices or connected passages.

Check first: Check every story path and keep an exported backup.

Access: Free open-source browser and desktop tool. Publishing or hosting the resulting story is a separate decision.

Open Twine: an interactive story · Full context and source

OBS Studio: record a demonstration

Consider it when: You want to show a process actually being performed.

Check first: Use approved sample material and inspect the recording for private details.

Access: Free open-source recording software for supported Windows, macOS, and Linux systems. A microphone or camera is optional by project.

Open OBS Studio: record a demonstration · Full context and source

Shotcut: a small video edit

Consider it when: A short sequence of clips needs a straightforward edit.

Check first: Review the complete exported sound and picture.

Access: Free open-source editor for supported Windows, macOS, and Linux systems. Media, storage, and processing requirements still apply.

Open Shotcut: a small video edit · Full context and source

Kdenlive: a more layered edit

Consider it when: The project genuinely needs a more layered editing workflow.

Check first: Test a short sequence before committing a large project.

Access: Free open-source video editor on supported desktop platforms; device capability and storage affect practical use.

Open Kdenlive: a more layered edit · Full context and source

W3C: accessible audio and video

Consider it when: The result includes audio or video someone else needs to understand.

Check first: Plan the appropriate captions, descriptions, and transcript before publication.

Access: Free public guidance; creating and checking accessible media still takes work and may require tools or assistance.

Open W3C: accessible audio and video · Full context and source

From choice to use

Keep the human purpose visible.

Keep an original thought

Use your own rough wording as the reference. Optional AI assistance can suggest a structure, but must not invent memories, quotations, or results.

Finish something deliberately small

A short example, captioned clip, or interactive vignette can be complete. Publishing more often is not the reason to begin.

Separate illustration from evidence

A fictional scene or conceptual visual can be useful when labeled. It must not masquerade as a recorded event or a personal demonstration.

Published as a selection path, not a personal field note. Source dates and access limits belong to each resource. No paid placement or affiliation is implied.
